::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## Core rule

Approval and publication are separate actions. Approval identifies the exact
reviewed candidate; publication verifies and promotes that payload without
recalculation.

## Current actions

| Workflow | Approval | Analytical publication |
|---|---|---|
| CVD events | **Update CVD events dashboard > Step 5**, approval action | **Step 6: Publish approved outputs** |
| CVD mortality | **Update CVD mortality dashboard > Step 5: Approve reviewed mortality release** | **Step 6: Publish approved mortality outputs** |
| Annual CVD report | **Annual CVD report > Step 2: Approve annual report candidate** | **Step 3: Publish approved annual report** |
| One-off CVD report | **One-off CVD report publication > Step 2: Approve one-off report candidate** | **Step 3: Publish approved one-off report** |

The rolling three-month update is a one-step build from exact approved event and
mortality releases. It does not introduce another analytical approval.

## Before approval

- Complete analytical, QA and disclosure review.
- Confirm product identity, period, version and source releases.
- Confirm the candidate and manifest are complete.
- Identify the authorised approver using a standing BNR role.
- Keep the candidate and review evidence in private controlled storage.

## Before publication

- Select the same identity and version that were approved.
- Require a valid approval record and matching manifest or fingerprint.
- Read from the controlled public-ready payload only.
- Stop if a file, identity, checksum or required confirmation differs.
- Confirm successful post-copy verification.

## After analytical publication

Inspect the authoritative public package and its website mirror. Quarto may then
present approved files, and GitHub may deploy reviewed public-safe website
source. Neither action substitutes for analytical approval or publication.

If any approved content must change, correct the source or version-controlled
code, create the required new version or authorised replacement, and repeat
review and approval. Never overwrite or manually repair the generated payload.
